title: Compactly supported direct image along an open immersion is extension by zero, for Weil sheaves
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $k$ an algebraic closure of $k_0$, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ a prime; put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers; def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For a $k_0$-scheme $T$, put $\bar T=T\times_{k_0}k$ and let $F_T$ be its geometric Galois Frobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On $\bar T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathcal R_{\bar T}$ be the sheafification of the ring presheaf sending $V$ to the continuous functions $|V|\to\Omega$ whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-subspace, with pointwise operations and restriction by precomposition. Let $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R_{\bar T})$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $\mathcal W_T=\mathcal A_T^{F_T^*}$ be the category of fixed pairs [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]: objects are $(M,\theta:F_T^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ and morphisms commute with $\theta$. A module is constructible if Zariski locally it admits a finite partition by locally closed subschemes on which its restriction is pro-etale locally finite free over the restricted coefficient sheaf. Write $\mathrm{WC}_{\mathrm{der}}(T)$ for the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal W_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on bounded objects with constructible underlying cohomology sheaves, and $\mathrm{WS}(T)$ for the full subcategory of $\mathcal W_T$ on constructible modules. Here $G[0]$ means the image in $D(\mathcal W_T)$ of the cochain complex equal to $G$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. These are the upstream Lean categories `ProEtaleWeilSheaf`, `WeilComplex` and `WeilSheaf`; this definition forms fixed pairs before deriving.

For an open $k_0$-immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow T$, let $a_{\mathrm W!}:\mathcal W_S\to\mathcal W_T$ be extension by zero of modules on the geometric fibers, with structure $F_T^*\bar a_!M\cong\bar a_!F_S^*M\xrightarrow{\bar a_!\theta}\bar a_!M$; the first isomorphism is reindexing the extension-by-zero construction along the Frobenius automorphisms. Denote its termwise functor on derived categories by $D(a_{\mathrm W!})$. For a $k_0$-morphism $u:S\to T$, $u_{\mathrm W*}$ is the ordinary direct image of these module sheaves, with the corresponding Frobenius structure, and $Ru_{\mathrm W*}$ denotes its total right derived functor on $D(\mathcal W_S)$.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open $k_0$-immersion, with $X$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and locally of finite type over $k_0$. For a compactification $c=(U\xrightarrow{a}Z\xrightarrow{p}X)$ [def-nagata-compactification], set $Rj_{\mathrm W!}^{c}=Rp_{\mathrm W*}\,D(a_{\mathrm W!})$. Let $Rj_{\mathrm W!}$ be this functor for the compactification selected in the upstream `WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek`, restricted to $\mathrm{WC}_{\mathrm{der}}(U)$. For every $G\in\mathrm{WS}(U)$ there is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{WC}_{\mathrm{der}}(X)$,
$$
Rj_{\mathrm W!}(G[0])\ \cong\ (j_{\mathrm W!}G)[0].
$$
Thus this is precisely the assertion of `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.nonempty_derivedLowerShriek_toComplex_iso_of_isOpenImmersion` for its actual upstream categories.

proof.text: Let c be the compactification selected by derivedLowerShriek for j. Its open map c.i is quasi-compact by Compactification.quasiCompact_openImmersion, since j is quasi-compact. The structure maps of U and c.Z are finite type by composition with j and the proper map c.g. All maps are over k_0 by Compactification.over and its existing IsOver instances. Thus the square with top c.i, bottom j, left identity of U and right c.g satisfies every hypothesis of the native proper/open interchange; its commutativity is c.comm.

proof.text: Apply native proper/open interchange to obtain a natural isomorphism from inclusion followed by R(id_U)_* and D(j_!) to inclusion followed by D(c.i_!) and R(c.g)_*. The latter composite is the chosen compact-support functor followed by inclusion, definitionally. The identity comparison in nativeWeilBasicComparisons removes R(id_U)_*. This proves the private nonempty_openShriekComparison, valid on every native Weil complex on U.

proof.text: Evaluate the inverse of this comparison at G[0]. Compose with the exact-functor single-object comparison mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor for the native extensionByZero. Its target is the degree-zero complex of WeilSheaf.extensionByZero j G, by the definitions of the two full-subcategory lifts. ObjectProperty.isoMk regards the resulting ambient isomorphism as an isomorphism of native Weil complexes. The statement prescribes no comparison morphism, so these components give exactly its Nonempty witness.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedLowerShriek_toComplex_iso_of_isOpenImmersion (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] [j.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (G : WeilSheaf k₀ l U) :
    Nonempty ((derivedLowerShriek k₀ l j).obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj G) ≅
      WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj ((WeilSheaf.extensionByZero j).obj G)) :=
  sorry
